knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Compacted fill and poor drainage must be tested and prepared before planting. Any change to the design is agreed with the client first.
Planting at the container depth with the crown above the finished soil avoids crown rot and root suffocation.
Mature size, root spread and proximity to services are checked, and a qualified arborist advises on a tree close to a sewer or building before planting.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock planting bed with a test hole, the learner records the soil type, topsoil depth and drainage observation within the assessor's set time.
The learner plants a supplied mock shrub at the correct depth, checks the crown height against the soil line and backfills and waters in without air pockets.
The learner completes a plant list for a supplied mock site, recording the mature size, the restriction check and the service distance for each plant.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Soil and drainage record for the mock bed, signed by the assessor.
Assessor observation record of the planting depth check.
Plant list with the restriction and service checks, reviewed by the assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Planting into the mock compacted fill without the preparation check during the assessment.
Burying the crown of a mock plant during the assessment.
Supplying a mock species marked restricted on the assessor's card.
